item.title: She spent 10 months restoring a 160-year-old house; now Lauren Iraeta is reconnecting families...
item.description: Lauren Iraeta approached her home renovation as a journey through time, merging creativity with historical inquiry. By delving into neglected family records and tales from earlier occupants, she uncovered names etched within the widow's walk. This captivating endeavor brought descendants closer to their ancestors' cherished childhood narratives, illuminating the profound history woven into these aged abodes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In June 2026, Washington began restoring 270 acres across two river islands; the project will...
item.description: In June 2026, heavy machinery commenced work on a significant coastal restoration initiative. The plan involves the dismantling of outdated sea defenses and the breaching of river levees on two islands, aiming to transform 270 acres of previously cultivated land into natural intertidal wetlands. This restoration will create critical habitats for juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon, with the completion date set for autumn 2028.

item.title: Meet Scarlett Tiani, the Connecticut student whose dog-safety invention reached US Nationals
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, Connecticut student Scarlett Tiani has garnered national attention for her inventive pet safety solution, Tail Wag Warning. Designed to enhance safety during unexpected dog interactions, Tiani's creation received numerous accolades at the prestigious national Invention Convention. With legal support at her side, she is now set to embark on the journey of securing a U.S. patent for her groundbreaking invention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Jimmy Chilimigras, the Mississippi teen who finished high school at 12
item.description: At just 18 years old, James Chilimigras has achieved remarkable academic milestones, having graduated from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law, where he ranked in the top two percent of his class while earning five certificates. Displaying an exceptional intellect, he completed both his bachelor's and master’s degrees by the age of 15 and became the youngest Certified Public Accountant in history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan's historic Ford House is replacing concrete shoreline with natural habitat
item.description: A groundbreaking initiative along Michigan's Lake St. Clair is reshaping the shoreline into thriving natural wetlands. By dismantling decades of concrete barriers, this project endeavors to create essential habitats for local fish populations. The transformation revolves around the historic Edsel and Eleanor Ford Estate, aiming to revitalize coastal marshes while boosting biodiversity and community education on ecosystem preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Elizabeth Hird bought Outer Island in 1964; in 1995, she donated it for wildlife, research and education
item.description: Outer Island, once a charming summer getaway, has been transformed into a vital protected wildlife refuge. The island was generously donated to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service by Elizabeth Hird in 1995, with the intention of preserving its natural resources and fostering education and research. Today, it serves as an invaluable living laboratory for students and researchers alike, ensuring a sustainable conservation legacy for generations to come.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New Jersey begins restoration work to bring back forest and wetland habitat along Raritan river
item.description: A 112-acre restoration project has begun along New Jersey's Raritan River to restore floodplain forest, wetlands and wildlife habitat affected by past contamination linked to the American Cyanamid Superfund Site. The project will plant about 50,000 native trees and shrubs, create three acres of vernal pools, control invasive plants and protect new vegetation with deer fencing. The restored site will be monitored and managed for 15 years.

item.title: Engulfed in flames, smoke: 2 killed as Russia hits passenger train with 340 onboard, says Zelenskyy
item.description: A Ukrainian passenger train in the Odesa region fell victim to a Russian drone strike, leading to the unfortunate demise of the driver and assistant. Simultaneously, Ukrainian military forces conducted a successful operation against a large oil refinery in Bashkortostan, causing extensive fire damage. This series of events serves as a stark reminder of the ongoing hostilities plaguing the region.

item.title: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient after raising funds for muscular dystrophy
item.description: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient at eleven years old. She received the honour for her extensive fundraising and awareness work. This recognition celebrated her dedication to Muscular Dystrophy UK and the disabled community. Carmela's journey began after her diagnosis with a rare muscle-wasting condition at age four. Her continued advocacy aims to promote accessibility and support for those affected.

item.title: In 2022, Buffalo completed the first emerald shiner passage on the Niagara River; four years later...
item.description: The city of Buffalo is enhancing a fish passageway to facilitate the journey of emerald shiners to Lake Erie. By installing steel baffles along the seawall, this initiative aims to mitigate strong currents. This effort is part of a significant multi-million-dollar restoration project for the Niagara River Area, alongside transforming nearby industrial slips into crucial shallow-water habitats, all geared towards rectifying historic environmental harm in western New York.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Washington launches project to restore 270 acres of Skagit estuary habitat
item.description: In a significant environmental effort, the restoration of 270 acres of estuary habitat in the South Fork Skagit River is underway, starting from June 2026 and set to finish by fall 2028. This initiative focuses on enhancing the habitat for the endangered Puget Sound Chinook salmon, ensuring a sustainable ecosystem by reconnecting islands to tidal flows, and supporting various wildlife, including waterfowl and shorebirds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 70 million years ago, Earth had 372 days a year, with days lasting 23 hours
item.description: Research into ancient shells has unveiled that Earth experienced a 372-day year around seventy million years ago. During the Cretaceous period, each day was approximately twenty-three hours and thirty-one minutes long. This study also examined the ancient Earth-Moon distance and revealed warmer ocean temperatures, with evidence of photosymbiosis. The mollusc fossil indicates it thrived for over nine years on a tropical seabed.
